reasons: Lake identity is verified for case_name "Pembaur v. City of Cincinnati", court "U.S. Supreme Court", date_decided "1986-03-25", and year 1986.
Lake citations list official cite "475 U.S. 469", vendor cite "1986 U.S. LEXIS 33", and parallel cites "106 S. Ct. 1292", "89 L. Ed. 2d 452", and "54 U.S.L.W. 4289".

The opinion frames the case as a Section 1983 municipal-liability refinement of Monell: "The question presented is whether, and in what circumstances, a decision by municipal policymakers on a single occasion may satisfy this requirement."
The home role "Key — Progeny / Refinement" is supported by the opinion's repeated Monell analysis and its holding that municipal liability may rest on a qualifying single policymaker decision.
residual_risks: No separate home-page file was disclosed; role support is verified from the case text and lake record only.

reasons: The holding is supported by the opinion: "municipal liability may be imposed for a single decision by municipal policymakers under appropriate circumstances."

The opinion states the limiting qualifier: liability attaches only where the decisionmaker has "final authority to establish municipal policy with respect to the action ordered" and where the official is responsible for final policy on the subject matter.
residual_risks: The lead opinion states it was the opinion of the Court except as to Part II-B; the disclosed treatment scope note nevertheless says the final-policymaker single-decision rule is settled law.
